Title: Welcome to Order Picking
Description: Order picking is the process of retrieving specific products from their storage locations in the warehouse to fulfil a customer order. It is the most labour-intensive activity in any fulfilment operation, accounting for 50 to 75 percent of total warehouse operating costs. Picking accuracy directly affects customer satisfaction — every mis-pick results in a return, a reshipping cost, and a dissatisfied customer. In this module you will learn how to read a pick list, locate and verify the correct product, pick the correct quantity, and handle errors before they leave the warehouse floor.
name: M1_01_Welcome_Order_Picking

Title: The Pick List — Your Instruction Sheet
Description: Every picking task begins with a pick list — either printed or displayed on a handheld scanner. Your virtual pick list appears on the wrist panel of your left hand. Open it now by raising your left wrist. The pick list shows you four pieces of information for each item: the SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) — a unique product identifier, the product description, the storage location (aisle, shelf, and bin number), and the quantity required. Read each line carefully before you move. Picking the wrong item or wrong quantity is far more costly than taking an extra few seconds to verify.
name: M1_02_Pick_List_Introduction

TutorialChallengeLists.ChallengeTitle: Open the Wrist Pick List Panel

Title: Reading Your First Pick — Location
Description: Your first pick list has one item. The location shown is A-02-03, which means Aisle A, Shelf 2, Bin 3. Warehouse locations follow this structure in most facilities: the letter identifies the aisle, the first number identifies the shelf level from the floor (1 is ground level, 2 is mid-level, 3 is top), and the second number identifies the bin position along the shelf from left to right. Aisle A is the first aisle on your left. Walk there now and find the correct shelf and bin before touching anything.
name: M1_03_Reading_Pick_Location

Title: SKU Verification — Never Pick on Description Alone
Description: You are now at the correct bin. Before you pick the item, you must verify its SKU. Product descriptions can be similar or abbreviated in ways that create confusion — for example, a bin labelled 'Blue Widget 500ml' may sit next to 'Blue Widget 750ml'. The SKU eliminates that ambiguity. Use the virtual scanner on your right hand — grip the scanner tool from your hip, point it at the item's barcode label on the shelf face, and press trigger to scan. The scanner will confirm a match in green or flag a mismatch in red. Only pick the item after a green confirmation.
name: M1_04_SKU_Verification

TutorialChallengeLists.ChallengeTitle: Scan and Verify the Item SKU

Title: Picking the Correct Quantity
Description: The pick list asks for 3 units of this item. The bin contains a mixture of this product and a similar-looking product. Count carefully before picking — do not grab a handful and assume. In real warehouse operations, quantity errors are the second most common type of mis-pick after wrong SKU, and they are harder to detect downstream because the product description may match. Pick exactly 3 units and place them into the virtual tote on your left side. The tote will count each item as it is placed.
name: M1_05_Quantity_Pick

TutorialChallengeLists.ChallengeTitle: Pick Exactly 3 Units into the Tote

Title: Multi-Line Order — Planning Before Moving
Description: Your next pick list has 3 items across two aisles — Aisles B and C. Before you move, read all three lines and plan your route. The most efficient approach is to pick all items in one aisle before moving to the next. Do not pick in pick list order if the order sends you back and forth between aisles — the pick list order is generated by the customer, not by your warehouse layout. Check the aisle, shelf, and bin for all three items, decide the most efficient sequence, and then start moving. The AI will record your route.
name: M1_06_Multi_Line_Order

TutorialChallengeLists.ChallengeTitle: Complete All 3 Picks in the Multi-Line Order

Title: Error Recovery — Catching a Mis-Pick
Description: Before you submit your tote, the system has flagged a potential error. One of the items in your tote does not match the pick list. This is a deliberate training scenario — in a real facility, mis-picks are caught at the packing station or, worse, by the customer. Your job is to check each item in the tote against the pick list, identify the incorrect item, remove it, and replace it with the correct one. Mis-picks that reach the customer cost an average of 12 to 15 times more to resolve than mis-picks caught on the warehouse floor.
name: M1_07_Error_Recovery

TutorialChallengeLists.ChallengeTitle: Identify and Remove the Incorrect Item

Title: Path Efficiency Review
Description: Your picking session is complete. The AI has now analysed your route through the warehouse and compared it to the optimal path. On the floor you can see two overlaid lines — a green line showing the optimal route, and an amber line showing your actual route. Every metre of unnecessary travel in a warehouse adds up across a shift. A picker walking 15 kilometres per shift who reduces their travel by 15 percent saves over 2 kilometres of walking per day. Study the difference between your route and the optimal route before continuing. The AI will highlight specific points where you backtracked or visited zones out of sequence.
name: M1_08_Path_Efficiency_Review

Title: Order Picking Assessment
Description: You have completed all practical stages of the Order Picking module. Now test your understanding with a 13-question knowledge assessment. The questions cover pick list reading, location codes, SKU verification, quantity accuracy, and error recovery. A score of 80 percent or above is required to pass. Apply what you have practised — each question is drawn directly from the scenarios you completed in this module.
name: M1_09_Assessment

Title: Module 1 Complete — Well Done
Description: Congratulations on completing the Order Picking module. You have learned how to read a pick list, navigate to a storage location, verify a product by SKU, pick the correct quantity, recover from a mis-pick error, and review your route for efficiency. These are the core skills of every picker on this floor. The habits you build now — verify before you pick, plan your route before you move, check your tote before you submit — will make you a reliable and efficient member of the team. Proceed to your next module when you are ready.
name: M1_10_Module_Complete
